name: Smile makeover / digital smile design

lead: A smile makeover redesigns the smile as a whole by combining treatments such as whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics into one plan. The aim is a changed colour, shape, size, alignment and display of teeth and gums.

Digital smile design is the planning step: photos and software, or wax mock-ups, preview the proposed look and apply proportion guidelines such as tooth width-to-length ratios. Clinicians assess facial features, tooth display and the gum line, then combine procedures to match the design, sometimes producing restorations with CAD/CAM. No clinical studies specific to smile makeovers were found.

paras: It usually runs as a multi-step programme with a design consultation, a preview or trial mock-up, then the chosen treatments in sequence. Timelines depend on which procedures are included.

Veneers and crowns usually require permanent removal of tooth structure. Cosmetic dentistry is not an ADA-recognised specialty, and critics raise overtreatment and marketing concerns. Costs are typically high.

angle.text: A smile makeover bundles whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics into one planned redesign, often previewed with digital smile design first. The new smile is visible once the work is complete.

lead: A smile makeover is a planned, often multi-step programme of cosmetic dental work that reshapes how the teeth and gums look as a whole: colour, shape, size, alignment and how much tooth and gum show when smiling. It may combine whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics, so the result is a brighter, more even and better-proportioned smile that suits the face. [1][2]

Smile design is the planning stage. A clinician assesses facial features, tooth proportions, how much tooth shows at rest and during a smile, and the gum line. A 2022 review describes smile design as creating an aesthetic smile from scientific and artistic guidelines, taking in facial esthetics, lip dynamics, gum and tooth esthetics and personality. [3] Digital smile design uses photographs and software to preview proposed changes before treatment; dentists have also long used wax or temporary mock-ups for the same purpose. [1][2][4]

Cosmetic dentistry is not recognised as a specialty by the American Dental Association. [1] A 2025 systematic review of seven studies reported that digital smile design improved patient satisfaction, treatment acceptance and communication compared with conventional planning. [5]

paras: Whitening is described as the most common cosmetic procedure, with options ranging from over-the-counter strips to in-office and supervised take-home treatment [1]. Bonding uses tooth-coloured composite to repair chips or close gaps, while porcelain veneers are thin shells bonded to teeth, usually with some irreversible enamel removal [1][2]. Crowns, bridges and implants replace or cover damaged or missing teeth, and gum contouring, clear aligners or braces may be added [1][2].

One encyclopedic source summarises commonly cited guidelines: about 3.5 mm of the upper central incisor visible at rest, decreasing with age; upper central incisor width-to-length ratios of roughly 75 to 80 percent; central incisors wider than lateral incisors; and a smile line that follows the curve of the lower lip. Golden-ratio approaches to tooth widths are also described [2].

The same source notes that its figures draw partly on dental-practice and consumer websites and are not all consistent, so these numbers function as descriptive conventions more than validated standards [2].

Digital workflows allow a patient to see a simulated result before treatment, and CAD/CAM systems are used to design and mill restorations. Reviews of dental technology describe digital design and manufacture as a major change in how restorations are produced.

A 2022 review explains that digital smile design analyses a person's smile from scanners and photographs and predicts how it can be modified, down to minor corrections. [4] A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of AI-based smile design tools reported improved smile symmetry, lip arcs and incisal edge visibility, and a pooled patient satisfaction prevalence of 58 percent with high heterogeneity. [6] A 2018 case report described a fully digital workflow integrating a dental scan, smile design and CAD-CAM. [7]
A case report describes a mock-up technique combined with digital smile design for planning porcelain laminate veneers. [8]

Critics cited in encyclopedic sources raise concerns about the use of the title cosmetic dentist without specific training, informed consent, overtreatment, the irreversibility of tooth reduction and marketing practices [1][2]. Prosthodontics and orthodontics are the recognised specialties most associated with aesthetic dentistry, while cosmetic-dentistry accreditation bodies are not recognised by the ADA [1].

Studies exist on the planning tools rather than on whole-smile makeovers. A 2025 systematic review of seven studies (randomized trials, observational and qualitative work) found that digital smile design improved patient satisfaction, treatment acceptance, communication and perceived predictability versus conventional approaches. [5] A 2025 meta-analysis of AI-based smile design reported aesthetic improvements and 58 percent pooled satisfaction. [6] A 2024 randomized comparison of traditional and digital crown extension guides in 62 patients with 230 anterior teeth examined clinical outcomes of aesthetic restoration. [9] A British Dental Journal article of 2022 reviews smile makeover treatments. [10]

timeline.event: Newell Sill Jenkins, regarded as a founder of aesthetic dentistry, develops porcelain enamel and advances porcelain inlays, crowns and bridges [1].
The American Society for Dental Aesthetics is founded [1].
The American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry is founded [1].
